newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Duma to vote on spending cuts May 23.
newsitem.headline: Russian Duma to vote on spending cuts May 23.

text.p: Russia's lower house of parliament, the State Duma, will vote on government proposals to cut spending on May 23, two days after ministers outline the plans, Duma speaker Gennady Seleznyov said on Thursday.

He said Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin would report on May 21 on 1997 budget spending and revenue and present plans to cut spending which had been drawn up by First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais. The vote would follow on May 23.
This meant a session on the results of Russian privatisation, originally scheduled for May 23, would be postponed by two weeks, Seleznyov added.
The bill to cut spending, known as sequestration, is likely to be the subject of heated debate in parliament, which is dominated by communists and nationalists.

The Duma on Wednesday ordered the Audit Chamber to verify the government's sequestration plan, which cuts planned spending by 108 trillion roubles. First quarter tax revenues were sharply below budgeted levels, and while tax income rose in April, it remained just 80 percent of planned levels.

Communist deputies have condemned the government's spending cut plans, and called for money supply to be doubled to ease the financial crisis. The central bank has rejected the idea, warning it could lead to hyperinflation.
